riddles.q: I have hands but cannot clap. What am I?
I am full of holes but I still hold water. What am I?
The more you take, the more you leave behind. What am I?
I have a face and two hands but no arms or legs. What am I?
What has to be broken before you can use it?
What gets wetter the more it dries?
I have keys but open no doors. What am I?
What can you catch but not throw?
What has a neck but no head?
What goes up when the rain comes down?

jokes: 😄 Why did the mbira player bring a pencil? Because he wanted to draw a good tune!
😄 Why was the maths book sad? It had too many problems!
😄 Why did the teacher wear sunglasses? Because her class was so bright!
😄 What is a cow's favourite subject? Moo-sic!
😄 Why can't a bicycle stand up by itself? It is two tired!

stories.b: Long ago, a small hare wanted to see the top of the great baobab tree. Every day he tried to climb, and every day he slipped. The tortoise said, 'Little friend, the baobab did not grow in a day.' The hare rested, practised a little each morning, and after many days he reached the top. From there he saw the whole valley shining. Moral: little by little, hard work takes you high.

Two girls carried water from the river. One had a pot with a small crack, so she lost water along the way. She was ashamed. But her mother showed her the path: flowers were growing all along it where her pot had dripped. 'Your crack watered the flowers,' her mother smiled. Moral: everyone has something that makes them special.

In dry season, a little bird could not find water. A big elephant dug the dry riverbed with his tusks until water came. The bird drank, and later she warned the elephant when a lion was near. Moral: kindness comes back to you, that is Ubuntu.
